# `silk/build/source`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Files of the package read while it compiles: shaders, tables and other data the program keeps
as part of its code.

## When to use
Use [`Source.read`](#Source.impl.read) for a file's bytes and [`Source.text`](#Source.impl.text) for UTF-8 text, from runtime code
or from a `static fn` that parses the file while the package compiles. Use
`silk.system.filesystem` for files the program reads when it runs.

## Details
The path is relative to the directory that holds the package's `silk.toml`, uses `/`
separators and has no `.` or `..` segment, so a package reads only its own files. Write it as
a string literal in the call: the build finds the files a package reads from those literals.
The file's contents become a constant of the program. Editing the file rebuilds only the
functions that read it.

## Examples
### Embed a shader
```silk,ignore
import silk.build.source { Source }

pub fn sceneShader() -> &'static [u8] {
  return Source.read("shaders/scene.wgsl")
}
```

Import as `Source` with `import silk.build.source { Source }`.

Public declarations: 1.

## `Source`

```silk
pub struct Source
```

The owner type of the package file reads. It has no fields and is never constructed.

### Details

Each operation is `static`: runtime code that calls one receives its result as a constant.

<a id="Source.impl"></a>

## Implementation `Source`

```silk
impl Source
```

<a id="Source.impl.read"></a>

### Associated function `read`

```silk
pub static fn read(path: string<'static>) -> &'static [u8]
```

Returns the bytes of the package file at `path`.

#### Gotchas

A path that leaves the package, or names no file, is a compile error at the call.

<a id="Source.impl.text"></a>

### Associated function `text`

```silk
pub static fn text(path: string<'static>) -> string<'static>
```

Returns the text of the package file at `path`.

#### Gotchas

A file that is not valid UTF-8 is a compile error at the call, as is a path that leaves the
package or names no file.
